items.title: Tier 0C-2 gate remains closed
items.statement: The registry explicitly keeps buildability false and disallows ordinary product WorkNodes and NodeSeeds; its authority is limited to Tier 0C-2 storage value contracts.

items.title: Launch-critical storage families are enumerated
items.statement: The registry names ten critical storage families, including approved plan packs, approval outbox rows, compile runs, compiler-wave contracts, drafts, requests, intake reports, attempt receipts, event indexes, blocked projections, and goal receipts.

items.title: ApprovedPlanPack persistence identity
items.statement: ApprovedPlanPack is a materialized Tier-0 launch-critical redb family keyed by project and pack identifiers, canonically MessagePack encoded, and owned by Planning Wizard PWIZ-014.

items.title: ApprovedPlanPack production and consumers
items.statement: The Planning Wizard final-review approval CAS produces the pack, while compilation bootstrap, implementation-readiness, and audit projection consume it.

items.title: ApprovedPlanPack closed value schema
items.statement: The pack value is a closed object with identity, version, lineage, index, context, policy, audit, creation, source-reference, and redaction fields required; optional PRD, amendment, closure, readiness, ledger, and supersession references are recognized.

items.title: ApprovedPlanPack validation constraints
items.statement: The schema fixes schema identity and version, requires nonempty string identifiers and hashes, positive versions and revisions, RFC date-time creation timestamps, arrays of nonempty source references, and one of two redaction profiles.

items.title: Pack recovery blocks stale hashes
items.statement: Recovery reads the pack by exact key, and stale hashes block launch and route the flow to Planning Wizard refresh.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Read by exact key during PlanApproved/PlanCompileRun recovery; stale hashes block launch and route back to Planning Wizard refresh.",

items.title: Pack migration and retention preserve lineage
items.statement: No legacy writer is canonical; future value changes require a new family version and preserved source-pack hash, and retained packs remain reachable through planning, audit, and GoalRun receipt lineage.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "No legacy writer is canonical; future value changes require a new family version and source-pack hash preservation.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain with planning-run lineage, audit closure, and any GoalRun receipt that references the pack; never compact below retained receipt reachability.",

items.title: Pack storage excludes secret-bearing bodies
items.statement: Only non-secret references and hashes may persist; project-context and policy bodies must remain referenced rather than embedded.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Only non-secret refs and hashes may be persisted; project context and policy bodies are stored by ref, not inline secret-bearing content.",

items.title: ApprovedPlanPack canonical crosswalk
items.statement: This value schema is canonical for Tier 0C-2 ApprovedPlanPack storage, while ledger and source-lineage pack prose is explicitly non-authoritative.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical Tier 0C-2 value schema for ApprovedPlanPack; ledger/source-lineage pack prose is non-authoritative.",

items.title: PlanApproved outbox persistence identity
items.statement: The PlanApproved outbox is a materialized Tier-0 launch-critical dual redb/seglog family keyed by project and idempotency key, canonically MessagePack encoded, and owned by Planning Wizard PWIZ-014.

items.title: Approval boundary feeds publication, compilation, and replay
items.statement: The Planning Wizard Approve And Build command boundary produces the row; EventRecord writing, PlanCompileRun binding, and idempotency replay consume it.

evidence.exact_quote: "Planning Wizard Approve And Build command boundary"

items.title: PlanApproved outbox closed value schema
items.statement: The closed outbox object requires schema identity, project, approval receipt, approved pack, idempotency, compile-run, status, sequence, creation, and redaction fields; publication ids, retry count, and last-error reference are optional and selected fields may be null.

items.title: Outbox state vocabulary
items.statement: The outbox status may be pending, published, acked, or failed.

items.title: Duplicate approval replay is idempotent
items.statement: A duplicate approval delivery returns the existing PlanApproved append/projection result for the same idempotency key.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Duplicate approval delivery returns the existing PlanApproved append/projection result for the same idempotency key.",

items.title: Outbox migration and retention
items.statement: Legacy unkeyed approval notes are source lineage only and migration first creates a keyed row; rows survive at least through compile-run and audit-closure retention, while failed rows keep retry lineage until superseded.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Legacy unkeyed approval notes are source-lineage only; migration creates an idempotency-keyed outbox row before publishing.",
"retention_compaction": "Retain at least as long as the referenced PlanCompileRun and audit closure; failed rows retain retry lineage until superseded.",

items.title: Outbox excludes approval and environment bodies
items.statement: The outbox stores only receipt identifiers, references, hashes, and status enums, not approval bodies or environment data.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "No approval body or environment data is stored here; only receipt ids, refs, hashes, and status enums.",

items.title: Outbox and EventRecord authority split
items.statement: The transactional outbox row is canonical for PlanApproved staging, while the append-only PlanApproved EventRecord remains the publication authority.

evidence.exact_quote: "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical PlanApproved transactional outbox row; PlanApproved EventRecord remains the append-only publication.",

items.title: Hash syntax and verification algorithm are unspecified
items.statement: Pack and index hash properties accept any nonempty string; the contract does not select a digest algorithm, byte encoding, canonicalization input, or comparison oracle, leaving stale-hash enforcement interoperably under-specified.
items.impact: Independent writers and readers can hash different bytes or accept malformed hashes, causing false stale-hash blocks or missed stale data.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose digest algorithms, canonical byte inputs, textual encoding, and validation behavior.

items.title: Outbox transition graph and commit boundaries are absent
items.statement: The schema enumerates four status values but does not define legal transitions, transition authorities, redb/seglog atomicity, when publication becomes visible, acknowledgement meaning, or crash recovery at each boundary.
items.impact: Implementations can diverge on retry safety, duplicate publication, acknowledgement, and recovery after partial writes.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent the state machine, atomic transaction boundaries, actor permissions, and recovery checkpoints.

items.title: Idempotency-key contract is too weak for replay authority
items.statement: The key is only constrained to a nonempty string even though it determines duplicate replay; derivation inputs, canonical form, collision scope, persistence duration, and mismatch handling are not specified.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Duplicate approval delivery returns the existing PlanApproved append/projection result for the same idempotency key.",

items.impact: Semantically different approvals can collide or equivalent approvals can miss replay, threatening exactly-once observable behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose key derivation, normalization, namespace, collision detection, and request-mismatch responses.

items.title: Retry mechanics and terminal failure policy are unspecified
items.statement: The row can record an unbounded nonnegative retry count and a nullable error reference, but there is no retry trigger, scheduling/backoff, attempt ceiling, poison-row handling, supersession procedure, or operator recovery oracle.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Retain at least as long as the referenced PlanCompileRun and audit closure; failed rows retain retry lineage until superseded.",

items.impact: Deployments can retry at incompatible rates, loop indefinitely, or strand failed approvals without a deterministic recovery path.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define retry classification, backoff and limits, supersession authority, and operator-facing recovery actions.

items.title: Reference fields and collections lack scale and locator constraints
items.statement: Several optional reference strings may be empty and reference arrays have no minimum, maximum, uniqueness, ordering, or URI/identifier syntax; source_refs require nonempty members but likewise have no collection bounds or uniqueness.
items.impact: Malformed or ambiguous references can pass validation, and unbounded arrays can create divergent serialization, lookup, and memory behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define reference grammar, empty-value handling, de-duplication, stable ordering, and size limits.

items.title: Outbox sequence allocation and concurrency semantics are missing
items.statement: outbox_sequence must be a positive integer, but allocation scope, monotonicity, uniqueness, gap behavior, concurrency serialization, and replay preservation are not defined.
items.impact: Concurrent writers can disagree on ordering or create duplicate sequences, affecting deterministic publication and replay.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose the sequence namespace, allocator, transaction boundary, uniqueness enforcement, and gap/replay rules.

items.title: No GUI contract belongs to this window
items.statement: The authoritative core defines storage families, producers, and consumers without any GUI-facing presentation, interaction, or user-visible state contract; GUI truth is not applicable to this storage-value window.

dimension_assessments.summary: Exact-key recovery, stale-hash launch blocking, duplicate replay, and storage behaviors are specified.
The registry enumerates critical families and materializes pack and outbox capabilities.
Required and optional pack/outbox value fields define persisted inputs and outputs, subject to reference-validation gaps.
Closed schemas and identities are strong, but hash, reference, idempotency, ordering, and dual-store transaction contracts remain incomplete.
Status vocabulary exists without a legal transition graph or authoritative commit boundaries.
Planning Wizard production authority, canonical crosswalks, and EventRecord publication authority are explicitly assigned.
Both materialized families point to Planning Wizard PWIZ-014 as owner documentation and name their producers.
Pack and outbox consumers span compilation, readiness, audit, publication, and replay.
This core is a storage-value registry and contains no GUI-facing contract.
Stale-pack routing and duplicate replay are specified, but outbox crash boundaries, retry policy, and failed-row recovery are not.
Both families forbid inline secret-bearing bodies and constrain redaction profiles, though hash syntax remains weak.
Pack propagation to compilation/readiness/audit and outbox propagation to EventRecord/compile binding/replay are explicit.
Retention lineage is stated, but retry scheduling, operator intervention, supersession, and dual-store recovery procedures remain unspecified.
No collection bounds, sequence allocation concurrency contract, or retry load controls are defined.
New family versions preserve source-pack hashes, legacy writers are noncanonical, and legacy approval notes migrate through keyed outbox rows.
Closed JSON-schema constraints and stale-hash blocking provide partial oracles, but no executable hash or state-transition oracle is specified.
Builders must choose hash semantics, outbox state/atomicity, idempotency derivation, retry policy, reference bounds, and sequence allocation.
The consequential unknowns are bounded to hash verification, dual-store transitions, idempotency, retry/supersession, reference grammar, and ordering concurrency.
